about: Toby's coding in the reflexive thematic analysis demo (working from home), invented. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: each extract as said with its codes, and the passage's note, or empty for a turn reviewed and left uncoded. make_demo_rta.py builds the workbook and the progress file from this and the interview CSV beside it.

extracts.text: my first day was me in my bedroom with a box.
I'm twenty-seven and I spend most of my life in one room.
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: That's my office and my bedroom and my living room
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: I open the laptop on the bed and I'm online by nine.
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: I go out and get a coffee from the place at the end of the road, walk round the block, and come back and sit at the desk like a person.
codes: Small rituals to start and stop

extracts.text: If my dot goes yellow, because I've been away from the laptop for ten minutes, I feel like someone's going to notice.
I'll get up to go to the toilet and I'll wiggle the mouse before I go.

turns.note: The dot stands in for a body at a desk. He knows nobody watches and does it anyway.

extracts.text: At home, all they've got is the dot and how fast you answer. So I answer really fast.
I'm never actually concentrating on anything, because I'm always waiting for the ping.
it means I sleep at work.
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: I started putting a t-shirt over it. Like a birdcage.
I can't put it anywhere else because there isn't anywhere else. So I cover it up.
I sort of go out as one person and come back as a worker.
codes: Small rituals to start and stop

extracts.text: on a bad day it doesn't start, it just sort of seeps in.
I'll see a notification from a client and I'll just reply. From bed.
the walk is the only thing that turns one into the other.
codes: Small rituals to start and stop

turns.note: A worker made each morning by a walk, as Ros is by her lanyard.

extracts.text: I take calls whispering sometimes.
I'm like, Mum, I'm working. And she's like, yeah, but you're at home.
codes: Others doubting it is real work

extracts.text: I learnt everything off a screen share.
I don't really know what a good marketing person sounds like. I've only ever heard them on Teams.

turns.note: Not missing a self he had, but never getting to make one.

extracts.text: And I ended up doing the whole thing from my car.
this is my big moment and I'm in a Fiesta outside a chicken shop.
I just felt like I didn't have a proper place to be a professional. Like I was pretending.
I miss the in-between bits.
Actually having colleagues, not just, like, names.
And not having to pay for the train.
it's a bit like being told you've won something you didn't enter. And then not being allowed to say you don't want it.
codes: A perk you can't complain about
